nodes.label: Q5: Nightly positions map red: topic naming
nodes.explain: Why do topic-name calls through the Codex CLI fail (149 of 867 topics on 2026-10-26, 555 of 988 on 2026-10-25, 442 of 844 on 2026-10-22), and why does the naming step take hours (18,690 s on 2026-10-26)? Settled by: Running settles the first part, not an evaluation: reproduce one failing call with the full Codex CLI stderr (the concern keeps only its first line). Reading settled why failures repeat: a failed topic is never written to the names file (tools/name_topics.py:79-87), the nightly run deletes the names file before naming (tools/nightly_sessions.py:81) and only names that were written carry over (tools/name_topics.py:51), so every topic that failed once is retried every night until a call succeeds. 867 is the number of topics in the build, not the number of calls; the nightly log does not record how many were carried. See docs/planning/next-plan.md step 1.

nodes.label: Q6: extract-or-run restart loop
nodes.explain: extract-or-run.service restarts every few seconds (NRestarts 2537 on 2026-10-27) because it is the older invocation of tools/extract_queue.py over private/extract_full_20261003/or_run with --budget 25 and no --contract. tools/finish_pipeline.sh:15 already reruns the same queue with --contract docs/capture_contracts/extraction-position-memory.json and INQUIRY_EXTRACT_MOVES=1, but it first waits for every extract-* unit to stop (tools/finish_pipeline.sh:12), so the looping unit also holds the finish pipeline back. Is anything in that queue unfinished? Settled by: Prior art settles the remedy: the contract and the contract-bearing invocation exist. Disable the unit; reading the queue's output folder settles whether anything is unfinished, and if so line 15 of finish_pipeline.sh is run alone (the whole script also renames every topic through the failing Codex route and publishes the map to personal-vps). See docs/planning/next-plan.md step 2.

nodes.label: Q14: Live checkout lags main
nodes.explain: How do merged fixes reach the code the jobs actually run? inquiry-graph-nightly.service, chatgpt-export-watch.service, extract-or-run.service and the brian-positions skill all run from ~/code/inquiry-graph, a symlink to the main checkout ~/code2/inquiry-graph, which on 2026-10-27 sat on main at 8672a4e (2026-10-15), 15 commits behind origin/main, with its own .venv. Its untracked uv.lock (2,559 lines) differs from the uv.lock that origin/main tracks since 8b063a0 (2,745 lines), so git refuses a fast-forward that would overwrite it. Settled by: Argument, no test: nothing local diverges (rev-list origin/main..HEAD is 0), and the only obstacle to a fast-forward is the untracked uv.lock, which differs from the tracked one. Compare the two files, move the untracked one aside (not delete), then git pull --ff-only and uv sync. The repeated update (from ship's post-merge step or the start of the nightly unit) must raise a keyed concern when the fast-forward is refused rather than fail silently. The other environments the jobs use (~/.venvs/inquiry-maps, tools/nightly_sessions.py:29; ~/.venvs/inquiry-or, tools/finish_pipeline.sh:15) need no sync for these 15 commits: the only pyproject.toml change since 8672a4e adds a dev dependency group and code2check settings, no runtime dependency. The next plan does this as step 0 with a done-when line.
